main_text.p: Sax. enim, Captivitas ἁαρτυnunʒe, & ἁαρτynýoε.Captivus ἡeaρτulinʒ,bafl etiam Teut. Vinculum: batten, tenere. Kilian.

ἱarᴅo, Valde, Nimis] Nobis, eodem senfu, bard, & barolp: valde enim laborare, to labour bard, dicimus: ferió & agrè contendere, sive decertare, nobis barolp to strive or contend. Eopfe senfu, Belg. berε, bard; Germ. bart.
ꝑarman, Calumniis] Quod Latin. Læsio, Damnum, nobis barme, à Sax. ἡeaρnmε: per translationem, forte, Calumnia, quod ex eâ fama lædùtur, & damnum datur. Sax. autem calumnia, ἡeaρnmrρρæc.
- ꝑategon, Æmulatione] Affonat Sax. ἡaτian, odio habere, quod Teut. baten, & baeten.
ꝑatongon, Iracundiam] Quicquid fervens (quemadmodum Iracundia) Sax. ἡatɔ, nobis bot.
ꝑelmoot, & beltmoot. furor] Quod quis, tanquam impos animi, furore actus facit, in the bot mood factum dicimus, uti etiam in the man mood: bot autem, ut suprà in batongon, à Sax.

page.notes: Old-English and Saxon words in black letter are marked with bl in the source but rendered here as plain text; some Greek-like letters in Saxon words (ἁ, ἡ) are doubtful. Marginal marks at the right edge are not legible as notes.
